description: The finding catalogue of ARC-007 decision 2: every finding a drafting job's correction loop can give, by code, with its kind (error, warning, or person — decided by a person, never sent back), the rule it enforces by name, and the text of what is wrong and of the expected correction. {name} marks a value the check fills in. MOD-job-harness formatFinding writes a finding as <artifact>:<line>: <kind>: <what> [<RULE>] — <fix>.

findings.rule: AN ERROR MUST BE FIXED, A WARNING FIXED OR JUSTIFIED
findings.what: the answer cannot be read as one JSON object ({reason})
findings.fix: answer with one JSON object in the form the prompt asks for, and nothing else.

findings.rule: AN ERROR MUST BE FIXED, A WARNING FIXED OR JUSTIFIED
findings.fix: answer in the form the prompt asks for: {expected}.

findings.rule: A USE CASE REALISES NAMED REQUIREMENTS
findings.fix: use an existing name or remove the line.

findings.rule: AN EDITED FILE KEEPS ITS IDENTIFIER
findings.fix: keep {opened}.

findings.rule: EXACT DUPLICATES ARE FOUND WITHOUT A MODEL
findings.what: "{name}" restates the existing requirement word for word but is classed {class}
findings.fix: class it as duplicate of {existing}.

findings.rule: A REQUIREMENT HAS FIVE FIELDS
findings.fix: give it the {field}: name, rule, source with its date, occasion and check.

findings.rule: A REQUIREMENT NAMES ITS CHECK
findings.fix: add a line *Check:* naming the test that guards it, or how it is checked at review.

findings.rule: ONE STATEMENT PER REQUIREMENT
findings.fix: split it, or keep it and give a one-line reason.

findings.rule: A TEST STATES ITS EXPECTED RESULT BEFORE IT RUNS
findings.what: the case {case} states no expected result
findings.fix: state the expected result as its assertion, or as a line Expected: … for a user test.

findings.rule: A MODEL-DEPENDENT TEST IS MEASURED AS A RATE
findings.what: the case {case} depends on a model's answer and is judged on a single run
findings.fix: report a pass rate over a number of runs fixed before the first run, compared with the last release.

findings.rule: COMMIT TESTS CALL NO PAID SERVICE
findings.what: the case {case} runs on every commit and calls {service}, which charges per call
findings.fix: use a recorded or constructed response, and mark the case for the nightly run if it also needs the real call.

findings.rule: EVERY ARTIFACT NAMES ITS ORIGIN
findings.fix: name under Guards: the requirement, by its name in capitals, or the use case UC-<nnn> it guards.

findings.rule: A TEXT FROM A MAIL IS SEARCHED FOR THAT MAIL'S PEOPLE
findings.what: the text holds {hit}, found in the mail
findings.fix: leave the person out, keeping the technical content.

findings.rule: REPORT DATA LEAVES THE MAILBOX ONLY REWRITTEN WITHOUT PERSONS
findings.what: a checking participant found a mention of a person: {hit}
findings.fix: rewrite the passage without the person, keeping its technical content.

findings.rule: A CONFLICT IS DECIDED BY A PERSON
findings.fix: shown beside {existing} for a person to decide; not sent back.

findings.rule: A RENAMED REQUIREMENT IS WITHDRAWN AND ADDED
findings.fix: proposed as the withdrawal of {old} and the new requirement {new}; not sent back.

findings.rule: EVERY ARTIFACT HAS AN IDENTIFIER
findings.what: {name} is not an identifier of its kind
findings.fix: write it as {form}.

findings.rule: A REQUIREMENT HAS FIVE FIELDS
findings.fix: add the {field}.

findings.rule: A REQUIREMENT NAMES ITS CHECK
findings.fix: name the test file that guards it, or say how it is checked at review.

findings.rule: A REQUIREMENT HAS A REGISTERED SOURCE
findings.fix: name a source the product links in docs/sources.md, or link {source} first.

findings.rule: A RESOURCE'S TERMS ENTER AS A SOURCE
findings.what: the source names the resource entry {resource}
findings.fix: name the source its terms entered as, SRC-<slug>.

findings.rule: A USE CASE HAS ACTOR, PRECONDITION, FLOW AND POSTCONDITION
findings.fix: add the section {part}.

findings.rule: ONE USE CASE, ONE FILE
findings.fix: name the file docs/use-cases/UC-<nnn>-<slug>.md and begin it with its front matter.

findings.rule: DIAGRAMS ARE MERMAID IN MARKDOWN
findings.what: diagram stored as an image file ({target})
findings.fix: replace the image by the same diagram as a ```mermaid block in this file.

findings.rule: ONE ARCHITECTURE DECISION, ONE FILE
findings.fix: name the file docs/architecture/ARC-<nnn>-<slug>.md, its front matter naming id, title and forced_by.

findings.rule: AN ARCHITECTURE DECISION STATES CONTEXT, DECISION, ALTERNATIVES AND CONSEQUENCES
findings.fix: add the section {section} to the file.

findings.rule: ONE MODULE, ONE FILE
findings.fix: name the file docs/architecture/MOD-<slug>.md, its front matter naming id, title, realises, follows, uses and provides.

findings.rule: A MODULE STATES ITS RESPONSIBILITY AND ITS INTERFACES
findings.fix: state the responsibility under ## Responsibility and each provided interface under ## Interfaces.

findings.rule: EVERY ARTIFACT NAMES ITS ORIGIN
findings.fix: name the {origin} it comes from.

findings.rule: THE NAME IS THE ID AND IT SURVIVES
findings.what: withdrawn on {date} without the reason under ## Withdrawn
findings.fix: add the section ## Withdrawn with the reason as its first paragraph; the file and its identifier stay.

findings.rule: THE NAME IS THE ID AND IT SURVIVES
findings.what: {id} is withdrawn and stands outside the group Withdrawn
findings.fix: move {id} into the group Withdrawn.

findings.rule: EVERY TEST HAS ONE LEVEL
findings.fix: give the test one line Level: unit, component, system, release or user among its first 20 lines.

findings.rule: ARTIFACTS ARE ARRANGED IN NESTED GROUPS
findings.fix: write the groups as a nested list, two spaces per level, one item per line as - <item>.

findings.rule: A GROUP CARRIES NO IDENTIFIER
findings.what: the group title "{title}" looks like an identifier
findings.fix: give the group a title in words.

findings.rule: A GROUP HOLDS ONE KIND OF ARTIFACT
findings.fix: move {id} to the group file of its kind.

findings.rule: AN ITEM HAS ONE PLACE IN ITS HIERARCHY
findings.what: {id} is listed a second time (first on line {first})
findings.fix: keep {id} in one place.

findings.rule: EVERY HIERARCHY IS KEPT IN A GROUP FILE OF ITS OWN
findings.fix: list only items of the product, by their identifiers.

findings.rule: A BACKLOG ITEM NAMES WHAT IT REALISES
findings.fix: name under realises: at least one requirement, by its name in capitals, or a use case UC-<nnn>.

findings.rule: THE BACKLOG LIVES IN THE PRODUCT REPOSITORY
findings.fix: keep the item as a file docs/backlog/ITM-<nnn>-<slug>.md of the product repository.
drop it, or say in one line how it differs from {id}.
